title: Perf bench scratch - KV cache & batching (Zoe Hart)
body:
Quick scratchpad for runs today (KV cache warm-up and batching impact). Objective: measure p95 latency and tokens/sec for rlhf-7b variants across batch sizes and seq lengths, check int8 quantized vs fp16, and note memory/GPU utilization. Using standard bench harness: bench/runner v0.9 (local infra: dedicated-dev pool, A100-80GB).

Checklist / notes to self:
- Warm caches for prefix-heavy workloads (chat-like).
- Use synthetic prompt generator (avg prompt len 40 tokens).
- Collect: p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, gpu_util, gpu_mem_gb, error_rate.
- Re-run failing configs with higher wall_time for stable tail latencies.

Commands used:
- python bench/run.py --model redwood/rlhf-7b-v2 --dtype fp16 --batch 1 --seq 512 --duration 120 --out run-7b-fp16-bs1-512.log
- python bench/run.py --model redwood/rlhf-7b-v2-int8 --dtype int8 --batch 8 --seq 512 --duration 120 --out run-7b-int8-bs8-512.log

Environment:
- infra: dedicated-dev-a100-80GB (auto-scaler off)
- runtime: 0.9.12, kernel selection: fused-attn for seq<=1024
- workload: chat prefix heavy (40 token prompt, gen 256 tokens)

Summary of important findings (TL;DR):
- KV cache warm-up matters: first 10 requests have ~20-30% higher p95 until kv cache filled for long convo simulation.
- Batching improves throughput significantly (tokens/sec), but p95 tail increases nonlinearly for batch >= 8 on seq>=512.
- int8 quantized shows ~1.6x tokens/sec vs fp16 at similar p95 for small batches (bs<=4); for large batches int8 memory win allows higher batch but tail p95 still grows.

ASCII chart (throughput vs batch size, seq=512, model=7b-int8):
batch | tokens/sec
1     | 420
2     | 760
4     | 1300
8     | 1850
16    | 2100  (note: p95 spike)

Detailed run notes (raw):
- run-2026-03-17-09:12 | model=redwood/rlhf-7b-v2 fp16 | seq=512 bs=1 | p50=38ms p95=118ms p99=240ms | tokens/sec=350 | gpu_util=62% | gpu_mem=42GB | err=0
- run-2026-03-17-09:40 | model=redwood/rlhf-7b-v2 fp16 | seq=512 bs=4 | p50=95ms p95=210ms p99=480ms | tokens/sec=980 | gpu_util=78% | gpu_mem=45GB | err=0.2% (OOM-retries: 1)
- run-2026-03-17-10:05 | model=redwood/rlhf-7b-v2-int8 | seq=512 bs=4 | p50=72ms p95=160ms p99=360ms | tokens/sec=1550 | gpu_util=81% | gpu_mem=28GB | err=0
- run-2026-03-17-10:30 | model=redwood/rlhf-7b-v2-int8 | seq=512 bs=8 | p50=160ms p95=420ms p99=920ms | tokens/sec=1850 | gpu_util=89% | gpu_mem=36GB | err=0.5% (retry backoff)
- run-2026-03-17-11:00 | model=redwood/rlhf-7b-v2-int8 | seq=1024 bs=8 | p50=320ms p95=860ms p99=1700ms | tokens/sec=1200 | gpu_util=91% | gpu_mem=42GB | err=1.2%
- run-2026-03-17-11:35 | model=redwood/rlhf-3b fp16 | seq=512 bs=16 | p50=110ms p95=260ms p99=640ms | tokens/sec=1700 | gpu_util=70% | gpu_mem=20GB | err=0

Observations / hypotheses:
- p95 tail grows quickly as batch increases because of stragglers + request serialization for large seq; investigate per-request scheduling (async vs sync).
- int8 shows clear memory advantage allowing bigger effective batch before OOM, but kernel selection for attention might be suboptimal for seq>=1024 (fallbacks causing spikes). Check kernel logs for fallback reasons.
- KV cache benefit: cold-start p95 is ~1.2-1.3x higher. For chat endpoints we should consider warm-up traffic or pre-populate cache for important customers.

Next actions (short):
- (HIGH) Add per-request timeline capture for worst 1% requests to identify serialization vs compute hotspots (issue PRF-312).
- (MED) Run a focused kernel-trace on int8 path seq>=1024 to find fallback kernels. Attach to GH PR.
- (LOW) Add a 'kv-cache warm' flag to bench harness to measure steady-state more quickly.

Notes to collaborators:
- Maya: can you re-run bs=8 int8 with --trace-kernel and keep wall_time=300s? Aim to capture p99 stabilization.
- Ethan: please check the autoscaler logs — noticed one OOM-retry that coincided with ephemeral infra spike at 09:36.

Links to outputs / raw logs:
- s3://redwood-perf/2026-03-17/run-7b-int8-bs8-512.log
- s3://redwood-perf/2026-03-17/run-7b-fp16-bs4-512.log

Rough recommendations for product/dev: (for discussion)
- Default hosted API: enable int8 model variants for non-sensitive workloads to improve throughput and cost. Need QA on quality delta first.
- For low-latency chat SLOs: default to batch<=2 for seq<=512, and implement fast-path cache priming for first request.

Random todo / open questions:
- Is there an easy way to simulate many small chat sessions (many prefixes) to stress KV cache invalidation patterns?
- How much of the p95 tail is network vs scheduling? Need to test colocated client to remove network variable.

End of scratchpad. Will clean up and push summarized findings to Confluence after Maya/Ethan follow-ups.
